title: Signal-fusion: Eval Fabrication & Telemetry Reconciliation Guide
author: Mira Patel
content:
SUMMARY
This guide describes a reproducible, service-aware workflow (Signal-fusion) for converting diverse runtime telemetry into deterministic, evaluable artifacts (fabrics) and synthetic workloads. These artifacts are used to reproduce, triage, and certify production degradations that involve multiple interacting signals (latency-quality coupling, quant regressions, KV-cache anomalies, routing fallbacks). The objective is to shorten time-to-root-cause and feed verified fabrics back into the eval-harness and regression-triage processes.

SCOPE
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private Redwood runtime deployments.
- Focuses on incidents where multiple telemetry signals co-occur and jointly explain customer-visible regressions.
- Excludes pure infrastructure failures (e.g., datacenter outage) unless they produce a measurable quality delta.

KEY DEFINITIONS
- Signal-fusion: merging latency, cache, embedding, tokenization, and routing signals into a compact incident fingerprint.
- Fabric (fabricated evaluation): a self-contained artifact that includes request payloads, RNG seeds, tokenizer metadata, arrival profiles, and model-variant matrix to reproduce a fingerprint under the eval-harness.
- Reconciliation: the process of mapping production telemetry to a minimal set of fabrics needed to explain observed regressions.

OWNERSHIP
- Owner team: engineering (Applied ML / Eval harness subteam).
- Primary author: Mira Patel (mira@redwood.com).
- Escalation: Runtime SRE oncall, Model Onboarding for model/quant issues.

WHEN TO RUN SIGNAL-FUSION
1) A fidelity or SLO alert triggers and the cause is not localizable to a single signal.
2) Telemetry shows correlated anomalies across signals (e.g., p99 spike + embedding cosine drop + fallback events).
3) Quant-shadow or shadow cohorts exhibit large deltas compared to baseline.

TELEMETRY SIGNALS -> FABRIC MAPPING (canonical)
- p99/p95 latency tail: synthesize short-burst replay preserving inter-arrival and concurrency distribution.
- token_error_rate / decode exceptions: include raw bytes, tokenizer version, and pre/post-tokenization checks in fabric.
- kv_cache_miss_rate: construct multi-turn contexts with preserved KV offsets and controlled warmup sequences.
- embedding_drift (cosine delta): include normalization steps, embedding model version, and seed inputs for batch replay.
- rerank_mismatch: mirror offline/offline reranker inputs in parallel harness to isolate ranking drift.
- fallback_count / routing events: run routing-policy simulator with constrained capacity to force failovers.

SYNTHESIS ALGORITHM (high-level)
1) Ingest: extract incident window (default 12h) from telemetry-bridge and traces.
2) Fingerprint: compute signature tuple {metric, dimension, severity, sample-set, implicated-models}.
3) Prioritize: score by user-impact * reproducibility index.
4) Fabricate: produce 1..N fabrics per fingerprint with: request-set (50-5000 samples), tokenizer metadata, arrival profile, model_variant_matrix.
5) Validate: run fabrics in fabric-runner (isolated eval-harness) capturing full telemetry.
6) Reconcile: if the fabric reproduces the fingerprint, attach fabric id to regression ticket and add root-cause hypotheses.

OPERATIONAL RUNBOOK (concrete steps)
1) Create a new fabric from an incident:
   Example CLI: rwdctl fabric new --incident=INC-2026-345 --window=12h --max-samples=500 --out=inc-2026-345-fabric.json
2) Manual review: open the artifact in Fabric UI and confirm tokenizer, KV offsets, and arrival profile.
3) Execute: rwdctl fabric run --file=inc-2026-345-fabric.json --env=staging-fabric --concurrency=4
4) Compare: rwdctl fabric compare --file=inc-2026-345-fabric.json --baseline=prod-snapshot-2026-02-25
   Acceptance: fingerprint similarity >= 0.8 for prioritized signals (example: p99 latency similarity >= 0.8 AND embedding-cosine correlation >= 0.75).
5) Escalate: if fabric identifies quant or model variant issues, open regression ticket and assign to Model Onboarding with fabric id and failing samples attached.

FABRIC JSON EXAMPLE (single-line for quick import)
{"fabric_id":"inc-2026-345","samples":256,"signals":["p99_latency","kv_miss","embedding_drift"],"model_matrix":[{"name":"rw-13b","variant":"fp16"},{"name":"rw-13b","variant":"q4_0"}],"arrival_profile":"burst-3-5s","seed":424242}

SYNTHETIC WORKLOAD CONFIG (recommended defaults)
- workload_name: inc-2026-345-burst
- arrival_profile: poisson-lambda=0.2s for 30s then cooldown 5s
- concurrency: 8
- sequence_length_distribution: short 60%, mid 30%, long 10%
- kv_warmup: prefill=True, prefill_sequences=20

QUALITY GATES & ACCEPTANCE
- Fabric reproduction gate: similarity >= 0.8 on prioritized signals.
- Root-cause confidence: high if implicated change explains >70% of delta in model outputs.
- Regression ticket mandatory fields: fabric_id, failing_samples (n<=50), suggested mitigations, targeted owner.

TRIAGE PRIORITIZATION MATRIX
- Severity A: p99 latency >2x AND quality delta >5% -> SLA: triage start within 4 hours.
- Severity B: p99 spike OR quality delta 2-5% -> SLA: triage start within 24 hours.
- Severity C: minor drift or infra-only footprint -> SLA: triage within 72 hours.

ESCALATION & INVESTIGATION CHECKLIST
1) Confirm instrumentation: timestamps aligned, tokenizer version, trace IDs.
2) Run fabrics against primary and quantized variants.
3) Quant-suspect pattern: fp16 passes, q4 fails -> run quant-shadow and notify quantization-profiles squad.
4) KV-driven pattern: reproduce with and without KV prefill; inspect context-slicing.
5) Routing/fallback pattern: simulate capacity constraints in route-sim and capture routing logs.

DASHBOARDS & METRICS (suggested)
- fabric-repro-rate by model and quant profile (target > 0.7).
- fingerprint-similarity heatmap (rolling 7d).
- open-regressions linked to fabric ids with repro status.

ONBOARDING CHECKLIST (for new services)
- Telemetry: ensure p50/p95/p99, kv metrics, embedding delta, token_errors are emitted.
- Trace propagation: request IDs surface in model logs.
- Tokenizer: store tokenizer checksum/version per request.
- Shadowing: enable mixed-fidelity shadow for 2 weeks before large rollouts.

ROLLOUT & ROLLBACK GUIDELINES
- Micro-canary: run fabric-anchored micro-canary (1% traffic) for minimum 48h with synthetic probes in shadow.
- Auto-rollback triggers: fabric-repro-rate < 0.5 OR production similarity to a known-broken fabric > 0.6.

APPENDIX: TROUBLESHOOTING EXAMPLES (short)
- Embedding drift + p99 spike after quant-profile rollout:
  Action: fabricate 1200 samples preserving normalization; reproduced on q4_0 only; root cause: per-layer scaling mismatch during quantization. Mitigation: pin quant-scale mapping and re-run micro-canary.

- Tokenization mismatch in a private deployment:
  Action: capture raw bytes from failing requests, reproduce tokenizer edge-case with v1.2; mitigation: enforce tokenizer checksum in deployment manifest and add pre-deploy tokenization check.
